segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now in Antioch, in the assembly there, there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said,

segments.speaker: God
segments.text: “Now set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then, after fasting and praying, they laid their hands on them and sent them off.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So, sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed to Cyprus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they arrived in Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. They also had John as their assistant.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After traveling through the whole island as far as Paphos, they came upon a certain magician, a Jewish false prophet named Bar-Jesus,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The proconsul summoned Barnabas and Saul and sought to hear the word of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Elymas the magician—for that is how his name is translated—opposed them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You who are full of every kind of deceit and every kind of fraud, you son of the devil, you enemy of all righteousness, will you not stop twisting the straight paths of the Lord?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And now, look, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind, not seeing the sun for a time.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Immediately mist and darkness fell on him, and he went about looking for people to lead him by the hand.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the proconsul, seeing what had happened, believed, astounded at the teaching of the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Paul and his companions put out to sea from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. But John left them and returned to Jerusalem.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They themselves went on from Perga and arrived at Pisidian Antioch, and on the Sabbath day they went into the synagogue and sat down.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Brothers, if you have any word of encouragement for the people, speak.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Israelites, and you who fear God, listen.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers, and he lifted the people up while they lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm he led them out of it.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For about forty years he put up with them in the wilderness.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And after overthrowing seven nations in the land of Canaan, he gave their land as an inheritance.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: All this took about four hundred and fifty years. After that he gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man from the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: After removing him, he raised up David to be their king, and of him he testified, ‘I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, who will carry out all my wishes.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: From this man’s offspring God, as he promised, has brought to Israel a savior, Jesus.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Before his arrival, John had proclaimed a baptism of turning back to all the people of Israel.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And as John was completing his course, he used to say, ‘What do you suppose I am? I am not he. But look, after me comes one whose sandals I am not worthy to untie from his feet.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Brothers, sons of Abraham’s family and those among you who fear God, it is to us that the word of this salvation has been sent.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For the people living in Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize him, and by condemning him they fulfilled the voices of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: Though they found no ground for a death sentence, they asked Pilate to have him put to death.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: When they had carried out everything that was written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But God raised him from the dead,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and for many days he appeared to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now his witnesses to the people.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And we bring you the good news about the promise made to the fathers:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: God has fulfilled it for our children by raising up Jesus, as it is also written in the second psalm: ‘You are my Son; today I have begotten you.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And as for his raising him from the dead, never again to return to decay, he has spoken in this way: ‘I will give you the holy and faithful things of David.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: That is why he also says in another psalm, ‘You will not let your Holy One see decay.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For David, after serving God’s purpose in his own generation, fell asleep, was gathered to his fathers, and saw decay,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: but the one whom God raised did not see decay.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So let it be known to you, brothers, that through this man forgiveness of sins is being proclaimed to you, and from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: by this man everyone who believes is justified.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So watch out that what is said in the Prophets does not come upon you:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: ‘Look, you scoffers, be amazed and perish, for I am doing a work in your days, a work you will never believe, even if someone describes it to you.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they were leaving, the people urged that these words be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the synagogue meeting had broken up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke with them and urged them to remain in the grace of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the following Sabbath almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when the Jews saw the crowds, they were filled with jealousy, and they contradicted what Paul was saying, speaking abusively.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first. Since you push it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, look, we are turning to the Gentiles.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For this is what the Lord has commanded us: ‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, so that you may bring salvation to the end of the earth.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord, and all who were appointed to eternal life believed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the word of the Lord spread through the whole region.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the Jews stirred up the devout women of high standing and the leading men of the city, roused persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and drove them out of their territory.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they shook the dust off their feet against them and went to Iconium.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

notes.note: The Greek word was the ordinary term for a civic gathering and the Septuagint's word for Israel assembled before God. 'Church' is the near-universal rendering and readers know what it refers to, but it now suggests a building or an institution. 'Assembly' is used throughout this translation so that the reader can see it is one Greek word.

Greek has one word-family where English has two: righteous and just, righteousness and justice, and the verb 'justify' are all the same root. The verb rendered 'justified' in verses 38–39 belongs to this family and means being declared or put in the right. Some scholars prefer 'justice' for the noun, as translations into most other languages do.

Paul addresses two groups: Israelites by birth, and non-Jews who attended the synagogue and honored Israel's God, some of them without becoming full converts. The 'devout' proselytes and women of verses 43 and 50 are described with a related term for worshipers attached to the synagogue. How fixed a category 'God-fearers' was is debated.

notes.traditional: suffered he their manners / put up with them
notes.note: Manuscripts are divided between two verbs that differ by a single letter: 'put up with their ways' and 'carried them as a nurse carries a child', that is, 'cared for them'. The same variation appears in the Greek text of Deuteronomy 1:31, which Paul is echoing. The SBLGNT reads the first; the evidence is closely balanced.

The same Greek word is rendered 'Gentiles' in verses 46–48. It means a people or nation, and in the plural it often means the non-Jewish peoples as a group. This translation chooses between the two English words by sense, as is standard practice.

notes.phrase: All this took about four hundred and fifty years
notes.traditional: after that he gave unto them judges about the space of four hundred and fifty years
notes.note: The Greek is simply 'for about four hundred and fifty years', and here it closes the preceding sentence, so the figure covers the time in Egypt, the wilderness and the conquest. Later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, place the phrase after 'after this', making it the length of the period of the judges. The earliest manuscripts support the order translated here.

The traditional 'repentance' now centers on feeling sorry. The Greek word, in Jewish usage, carries the prophets' call to return to God: a change of direction in mind and conduct. Most translations keep 'repentance' as an established term understood to include a change of life.

The earliest manuscripts read 'for our children', which the SBLGNT prints and which is translated here. Many scholars suspect an early copying error, since the sense expected is 'for us, their children', the reading found in later manuscripts and followed by most English versions. The question remains open.

notes.traditional: in that he hath raised up Jesus again
notes.note: The verb can mean raising someone from the dead or bringing someone onto the stage of history, as God 'raised up' David in verse 22. Most interpreters take it here of the resurrection, in view of verses 30 and 34; others think Jesus' appearance in Israel is meant, with the resurrection first addressed in verse 34. The translation leaves both possible.

notes.phrase: the holy and faithful things of David
notes.note: This quotes the Greek version of Isaiah 55:3, where the phrase refers to the lasting covenant blessings promised to David. The word 'holy' here is the same word as 'Holy One' in the next verse, quoted from Psalm 16, and the argument depends on that link. Many translations render 'the holy and sure blessings of David', which obscures the connection less than the older 'sure mercies'.

The adjective comes from the word for 'age'. In Jewish usage 'eternal life' is the life of the age to come, a matter of its kind as well as its unending length. A minority of translators render 'life of the age to come' throughout.

The verb means to assign or set in place, and the passive is usually understood to mean that God had appointed these people to eternal life. Some interpreters read the form as a middle voice, 'had set themselves toward' or 'were disposed to' eternal life, in contrast with those in verse 46 who judged themselves unworthy of it. The passive reading is the majority view and is followed here.

The verb and its noun recur everywhere and are variously rendered 'preach the gospel', 'evangelize', 'announce good news'; readers should see one family.
The word covers both slander of people and blasphemy against God, and translators differ verse by verse on 'blaspheme', 'revile' or 'slander'.
The noun means release or remission and recurs in key formulas ('forgiveness of sins'); 'forgiveness', 'release' and 'remission' all have defenders.
